module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1028

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1028](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1028)
- [Er63d] Erdős, Pál, *On combinatorial questions connected with a theorem of Ramsey and van der
  Waerden*. Mat. Lapok (1963), 29-37.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [ErSp71] Erdős, P. and Spencer, J., *Imbalances in $k$-colorations*. Networks (1971/72),
  379-385.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Asymptotics

namespace Erdos1028

/-- The imbalance of a finite set `X` under a colouring `f`, that is,
$\left\lvert \sum_{x<y\in X} f(x,y)\right\rvert$. -/
def imbalance (f : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ) (X : Finset ℕ) : ℤ :=
  |∑ x ∈ X, ∑ y ∈ X.filter (fun y => x < y), f x y|

/-- `H n` is the minimum, over all colourings `f` of pairs from `{1, …, n}` with values in
`{-1, 1}`, of the largest imbalance of a subset `X ⊆ {1, …, n}`. -/
noncomputable def H (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m | ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ, (∀ x y, f x y = 1 ∨ f x y = -1) ∧
    ∀ X ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n, imbalance f X ≤ (m : ℤ)}

/--
Let
$$H(n)=\min_f \max_{X\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}} \left\lvert \sum_{x<y\in X} f(x,y)\right\rvert,$$
where $f$ ranges over all functions $f:\{1,\ldots,n\}^2\to \{-1,1\}$. Estimate $H(n)$.

Erdős [Er63d] proved
$$\frac{n}{4}\leq H(n) \ll n^{3/2}.$$
Erdős and Spencer [ErSp71] proved that $H(n)\gg n^{3/2}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1028.lean"]
theorem erdos_1028 :
    (fun n => (H n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
      fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős [Er63d] proved
$$\frac{n}{4}\leq H(n) \ll n^{3/2}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1028.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) / 4 ≤ (H n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős [Er63d] proved
$$\frac{n}{4}\leq H(n) \ll n^{3/2}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1028.variants.upper_bound :
    (fun n => (H n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős and Spencer [ErSp71] proved that $H(n)\gg n^{3/2}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1028.variants.erdos_spencer :
    (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n => (H n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1028

reformulations.difference: erdosproblems.com/1028 writes the inner sum as $\sum_{x\neq y\in X} f(x,y)$, with $f$ ranging over functions $f:X^2\to\{-1,1\}$. The Lean `imbalance`/`H` sum over `x < y`, so each unordered pair is counted once. There `f : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ` is ±1-valued everywhere, and only its values on pairs 1 ≤ x < y ≤ n matter. The main docstring likewise says $x<y$ and $f:\{1,\ldots,n\}^2\to\{-1,1\}$.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The site's sum cannot range over ordered pairs with an arbitrary f. An antisymmetric f (f(y,x) = -f(x,y)) makes every sum 0, so H ≡ 0, which contradicts the recorded bound n/4 ≤ H(n). So the sum must range over unordered pairs {x,y}, i.e. the edges of K_n, which is exactly the Lean's x < y. This is also Erdős's own definition. [Er63d] (English summary): 'Let h(i,j), 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n be an arbitrary function which takes on the values ±1. H(G^(r)) = Σ h(i,j) where the summation is extended over all the edges of the subgraph G^(r) … H(n) = min max |H(G^(r))|'. [Er71, p.107, problem 24]: 'Let f(i,j) = ±1, 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n … the minimum is taken over all the 2^{C(n,2)} functions f(i,j)'. [ErSp71] define g_2 on 2-subsets W ⊆ {1..n} and sum over W ⊆ B. The Lean H is min_f max_X of this imbalance: the sInf set is upward closed and nonempty (checked in Lean: H n ≤ n*n). Under the other conceivable reading (ordered pairs, symmetric f), H doubles. That leaves the Θ, O and Ω statements unchanged, and the eventual bound n/4 ≤ H(n) stays true because it follows from H ≫ n^{3/2}. The linked formal proof (plby) also counts each unordered pair once (Sym2 (Fin n), non-diagonal).

sources_consulted: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1963-15.pdf (Erdős, Mat. Lapok 14 (1963) 29-37 [Er63d], incl. English summary; OCR text layer)
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-25.pdf (Erdős, Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis [Er71], p.107 problem 24; OCR text layer)
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-05.pdf (Erdős–Spencer, Imbalances in k-colorations, Networks 1 (1971/72) 379-385 [ErSp71]; OCR text layer)
review.notes:
No misformalization found. Declaration by declaration:

- `imbalance` and `H`: faithful to Erdős's definition (see the reformulation entry). I checked in Lean that the sInf set is nonempty (H n ≤ n*n) and that 1 ≤ H n for n ≥ 2.
- `erdos_1028` (H =Θ n^{3/2}): this is the accepted resolution of "Estimate H(n)". Erdős [Er63d] gives the upper bound and Erdős–Spencer [ErSp71] the lower bound; ErSp71 prove c_k n^{(k+1)/2} ≤ H_k(n) ≤ c'_k n^{(k+1)/2} for large n, and H_2 is exactly the file's H.
- `upper_bound` and `erdos_spencer`: the repo notation `g ≪ f` means `IsBigO atTop g f`. So these say H = O(n^{3/2}) and n^{3/2} = O(H), i.e. H ≪ n^{3/2} and H ≫ n^{3/2}. Both are correct and equivalent to the Vinogradov forms, since finitely many n can be absorbed into the constant.
- `lower_bound` uses `∀ᶠ` rather than 'for all n'. This is necessary, not a weakening of a true claim: the literal all-n reading of "n/4 ≤ H(n)" is false even in Erdős's own normalization.
  - At n = 1, H(1) = 0.
  - At n = 5, the pentagon colouring (C5 red, complement blue) gives every subset imbalance ≤ 1. I verified this with `decide` over the powerset of {1,…,5}, and proved `¬ (5/4 ≤ H 5)` in a scratch file.
  - Erdős's star argument (sketched in the Hungarian text of [Er63d]) actually gives ⌈(n−1)/2⌉/2 ≥ (n−1)/4.
  - The eventual statement is true because it follows from Erdős–Spencer. It is the natural reading of the source's asymptotic remark "n/4 ≤ H(n) ≪ n^{3/2}".
- Docstrings: the main docstring departs from the site's literal wording (x<y instead of x≠y, {1..n}^2 instead of X^2). This matches Erdős's originals and agrees with the Lean, so it is not a defect.
- Status: `research solved` plus the `formal_proof` attribute matches erdosproblems.com ('SOLVED (LEAN)') and the teorth database ('solved (Lean)', last update 2026-01-19). plby's Lean file proves ∃ c < C, eventually c n^{3/2} ≤ H n ≤ C n^{3/2}. Its H is the same up to relabelling Fin n ↔ {1..n} and Sym2 ↔ x<y.
- Access limits: erdosproblems.com itself is behind Cloudflare, so I read the rendered page through the 2026-07-09 Wayback snapshot. I could not fetch the LaTeX source, history or forum pages (Wayback and archive.ph rate-limited me). In [Er71] p.107 the displayed formula is image-only, and its OCR is garbled. None of this leaves any declaration unsettled.
